name: Eiffel Tower
description: The wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars, Paris's most recognizable landmark, with observation decks and evening light shows.

name: Louvre Museum
description: The world's largest art museum, home to the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo, housed in a former royal palace.

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
description: The Gothic masterpiece on Île de la Cité, undergoing restoration after the 2019 fire but still a defining Paris landmark to view from outside.

name: Musée d'Orsay
description: A former railway station turned museum, holding the world's largest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces.

name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
description: The white-domed basilica crowning Montmartre hill, offering one of the best panoramic views over Paris.

name: Arc de Triomphe
description: The monumental arch honoring those who fought for France, at the center of twelve radiating avenues including the Champs-Élysées.

name: Champs-Élysées
description: Paris's grand shopping avenue running from the Arc de Triomphe toward the Place de la Concorde, lined with flagship stores and cafés.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: The opulent former royal residence with its Hall of Mirrors and vast gardens, a short train ride outside central Paris.

name: Luxembourg Gardens
description: An elegant formal garden on the Left Bank with a central pond, statues, and shaded paths, popular with students and locals alike.

name: Latin Quarter
description: The historic student district around the Sorbonne, full of narrow medieval streets, bookshops, and bistros.

name: Le Marais
description: A trendy historic district of Paris known for its boutiques, falafel shops, art galleries, and pre-Revolutionary architecture.

name: Centre Pompidou
description: A modern art museum instantly recognizable for its inside-out architecture, with exposed pipes and escalators on the exterior.

name: Sainte-Chapelle
description: A Gothic royal chapel famed for its dazzling stained-glass windows depicting biblical scenes, tucked within the Palais de la Cité.

name: Montmartre & Place du Tertre
description: A hilltop artists' village with cobbled streets, portrait painters in the square, and the setting for much of Amélie.

name: Musée de l'Orangerie
description: An intimate museum best known for Monet's monumental Water Lilies murals, displayed in two oval rooms designed for them.

name: Canal Saint-Martin
description: A picturesque tree-lined canal with iron footbridges, popular for picnics, boutique shopping, and canal-side cafés.

name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
description: A vast, tree-shaded 19th-century cemetery and the final resting place of Jim Morrison, Chopin, and Oscar Wilde.

name: Seine River & Pont Neuf
description: Paris's oldest standing bridge and the classic starting point for a Seine river cruise past the city's major landmarks.

name: Rue Cler Market Street
description: A pedestrian market street near the Eiffel Tower lined with cheese shops, bakeries, and produce stalls, ideal for picnic supplies.

name: Jardin des Tuileries
description: A formal garden connecting the Louvre to Place de la Concorde, with fountains, sculptures, and a Ferris wheel in summer.

name: Musée Rodin
description: A museum in a former mansion showcasing Auguste Rodin's sculptures, including The Thinker, set in a rose garden.

name: Bois de Boulogne
description: A large wooded park on the western edge of Paris with lakes, gardens, and cycling paths, ideal for escaping the city bustle.

name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
description: Paris's oldest covered market, a food-stall hub in the Marais serving everything from couscous to Japanese bento.

name: Catacombs of Paris
description: An underground ossuary lining former limestone quarry tunnels with the remains of millions of Parisians, a unique historical curiosity.
